questions.q: Where do the RTO of 4 hours and RPO of 1 hour for Harrow Peak Outfitters actually come from?
options: A guess made by the engineer based on what seemed technically convenient
A business decision made by the Operations Manager, which then drives the backup design for each resource
A number copied directly from an unrelated company's disaster recovery plan
A default setting built into Azure Backup that applies to every deployment
questions.explain: RTO and RPO are business decisions stated by the Operations Manager; the backup configuration is built to satisfy them, not the reverse.

questions.q: Why does harrowpeak-orders-db use continuous transaction log backups with point-in-time restore rather than a daily backup like the app VM?
options: There's no real difference -- both resources use the exact same backup schedule
Because databases are never allowed to use daily backups in Azure
Because its 1-hour RPO requires restore granularity measured in minutes, which a once-daily backup structurally cannot provide
Because the app VM's data is more valuable and needs a lighter backup schedule
questions.explain: A 1-hour RPO means at most an hour of data loss is acceptable, which only a near-continuous backup method like point-in-time restore can satisfy.

questions.q: Why does this lesson actually perform three restores instead of just confirming the backup jobs completed successfully?
options: Because completed backup jobs are a legal requirement but restores are optional
Because restore testing is only required for storage accounts, not databases or VMs
Because Azure Backup jobs always fail silently without any error message
Because a backup job reporting success proves nothing about whether a restore will actually work -- only testing the restore does
questions.explain: A backup policy nobody has tested with a real restore is a backup policy nobody can actually trust, which is why all three get verified for real.

questions.q: During the final smoke test, a blob upload fails with a 403 error. What does checking the RBAC role assignment rule out, before the actual network-rule cause is found?
options: That the app was ever able to connect to the internet
That the managed identity is missing the correct permission -- the role assignment is confirmed correct, pointing to a different layer
That the storage account exists at all
That the VM has a valid managed identity assigned to it
questions.explain: Confirming the Storage Blob Data Contributor role is correctly assigned rules out a permissions problem, which is what directs the next check to the storage account's network rules.

questions.q: What distinguishes a handoff checklist written for the next engineer from documentation written just to remind yourself later?
options: It documents RBAC assignments, tested and dated backups, correct monitoring contacts, and honestly names any deferred items
It omits any open items so the environment looks fully finished
It's written after the next engineer has already started, not before
It only needs to list the Azure resource names, nothing else
questions.explain: A handoff checklist written for someone else states access, tested backups, monitoring contacts, and deferred items honestly, rather than leaving gaps implied.
